body:
# Independent audit: vanishing buffers and ordinary deepest-face exhaustion

Audited source: `candidate 36607dd22d2fb045`, Sections 1--6 including 4a and 5a. Its 663-check verifier was rerun and passed. The analytic arguments below are independent of those finite calibrations.

Also full-read: `candidate cebc39c4f5ccbc96`, Sections 1--7. Its exact body construction, uniform own-strip estimate, and extension to o(1)-optimal global values pass. The compact positive bad-sublevel and limiting minor-quota framework is an explicit hypothesis of that application; merely having a bad family on an arbitrary fixed base would not by itself imply it. The author applied this requested clarification in Section 6.



## 1. Audit of the existing limit source

The physical scale is correctly `h_j=epsilon_j^(d+1)L_j`. Positive-set parity and the limiting proper-minor quotas bound its sampled maxima, uniformly as epsilon tends to zero. This argument does not bound L_j itself. If a sampled maximum array diverged, a positive limiting concave array would select a base of atomic depth at least M/k. At that fiber's centroid, the nonnegative-concave centroid bound and E(g)=V make every continuous-direction buffer eventually capture all fibers with nonnegative base drift. This contradicts the strict buffered sublevel below 1/k.

The sampled interior compactness and the opposite-inner-ball maximum estimate are valid for merely convex positive fibers. They give the exact zero-fiber statement (9); no boundary equicontinuity is assumed. The logarithmic superlevel bound correctly forces some zero fiber. Concavity proves that the minimal base face of a zero fiber is entirely zero, without asserting that the whole zero set is one face or a closed minor.

The boundary-depth-zero argument uses a finite support-height LP. It supplies a finite ambient supporting plane with a NONZERO continuous normal. Thus its trace has zero d-volume on every sampled fiber even if several supporting facets coincide. Combined with the bounded physical scale and continuous zero-boundary extension of energy, this proves uniform own-source interiority. Uniform convergence of physical buffers follows by splitting off a common interior core and using uniform energy vanishing on the remaining collars. The all-normal slab estimate is independent of the base tilt, so it legitimately passes the infimum over all ambient caps and then the maximum over sampled marks.

Section 4a correctly uses sampled touching majorants, not an unproved ambient supergradient of the changing concave parameter. The own continuous gradients are bounded by the common source balls; fixed-matrix minimum-norm base slopes are then bounded. The old contact certificate forces equality of the finite minimum of those planes with h_j on all sampled fibers. This proves the claimed stronger uniform boundary convergence for these certified parameters. A limiting plane at a zero source has zero continuous gradient because its value there tends to zero while it is nonnegative on a common ball.

The original-volume rows in (12) have the right reweighting and have mass sigma, not one. Their sum is exactly normalized original volume. Positive-source rows give no limiting original mass to zero fibers by the displayed direct estimate (14). Zero-source rows remain on their source's minimal base face before taking the limit; reweighting does not alter that support. Hence the split and the finite cover (16a) are valid. The original rows are not martingales, and the source explicitly preserves this distinction.

Section 5a's opposite-continuous-cap argument gives, at every sampled mark,

    D_0(p,y) <= b_base(p) - V_p/2.                    (A1)

The two caps use the SAME large finite minimizing base tilt and opposite continuous normals. Their masses sum to twice the selected atomic mass minus the total mass on its zero-base trace. Closed continuous boundaries add no mass. This is correct even in base rank zero.

The equality chain in Section 6 correctly requires an INTEGER anchored target. Convexity of the buffered level region and strict atomic gap at every input give a deepest target with an attained own-proper active cap. Equality of its quantile inequality forces equality in both the parameter and energy concavity inequalities, with the proportionality stated in (18). The marked-energy equality theorem then gives the exact positive homothety ratio (19). This excludes mixing positive and zero limiting source classes and gives their closed-minor and disjoint-parity statements. It does not partition the target parities.

## 2. Strict increase from zero buffer without cap attainment

Here is a useful independent strengthening of the strictness step in 5a. Fix any sampled interior mark Y=(p,y), and write D_0(Y) for its ordinary raw depth. Let a positive scalar delta multiply a continuous norm Gamma(u). Assume Gamma is positive definite; for Euclidean unit u it has a lower bound gamma_*>0. Choose r>0 with B(y,r) contained in K_p.

Every nonvertical buffered cap through Y adds, relative to its unbuffered counterpart, the own-fiber slab

    -delta Gamma(u) <= u.(X-y) < 0.

Normalize ||u||=1. With w=min(delta gamma_*,r/2), this slab has volume at least

    c(r,delta)=w kappa_(d-1) (sqrt(3) r/2)^(d-1)>0,

where kappa_0=1. Thus every nonvertical buffered cap has mass at least D_0(Y)+c(r,delta). Every pure-base cap has mass at least D_0(Y)+V_p/2 by (A1). Taking the infimum yields

    D_delta(Y) >= D_0(Y)+min(c(r,delta),V_p/2)>D_0(Y). (A2)

No active-cap attainment, coarea differentiability, supporting-facet allocation, or strict atomic gap hypothesis is required. The own-interior hypothesis is essential. This also covers a scalar buffer depending on the mark, since the mark is fixed in the argument.

## 3. Exact isolation of an exposed base face

Let F be a nonempty face of Q=conv(P), and let S_F be the subfamily over P intersect F. At every actual point Y over F,

    ordinaryDepth_S(Y) = ordinaryDepth_(S_F)(Y),       (A3)

where the right side is computed in aff(F) x R^d with its relative halfspaces.

For one inequality, restrict any ambient cap containing Y to that relative space. It is either a containing relative cap or the whole relative space. Its captured mass from S_F is at least the relative depth.

For the reverse inequality choose any relative containing cap and extend its affine defining functional to the ambient space. Choose a base-affine exposing function e with e=0 on F and e>0 at every sampled base outside F. Subtract T e from the cap margin. Its trace on S_F is unchanged. Since there are finitely many outside fibers, all bounded, one FINITE T makes their margins strictly negative everywhere. The resulting ambient CLOSED cap has exactly the desired relative captured mass. Apply this to arbitrarily near-minimizing relative caps; neither limiting open caps nor an attained relative minimizer is needed. Pure-base relative caps and a singleton face are covered as well.

## 4. Ordinary local-minimum face-exhaustion lemma

Let a positive compatible canonical family have maximum ordinary raw depth Q_0>0 and deepest-base set I. Write F_p for the minimal face of Q containing p. If

    u in P outside union_(p in I) F_p,                (A4)

the family cannot be a local minimum of normalized ordinary depth among ALL positive compatible families on this fixed base.

Indeed replace K_u by K_u+t B_d, leave the other input fibers unchanged, and take their canonical convex hull. Denote its actual fibers by K_z(t). Then, for every z,

    K_z subset K_z(t) subset K_z+t B_d,
    K_u(t)=K_u+t B_d.                                (A5)

The second inclusion follows by writing each new hull point as an anchored combination of old fiber points plus lambda_u t b; the old combination belongs to K_z and 0<=lambda_u<=1. This gives an actual compatible family with exactly the same complete base set. Every K_z stays full dimensional. Its mixed mass strictly increases for t>0.

For every protected face F_p in (A4), an anchored representation targeting F_p uses only inputs in F_p. Since u is outside it, the entire face subfamily is unchanged. Formula (A3) shows that the ordinary depth at EVERY point over that face is unchanged, even though bodies elsewhere may have grown. In particular each old deepest base still has maximal raw depth exactly Q_0.

For completeness, no new deepest base can appear for small t. Put Delta_t=sum_z |K_z(t) minus K_z|=O(t); the O(t) bound follows from (A5) and the fixed positive convex bodies. Every x_t in K_z(t) is within t of K_z. Pair caps at x_t with caps at a nearest old x, normalize the continuous normal to Euclidean length one, and use the uniform section-area slab bound. Independently of the base tilt,

    |depth_t(z,x_t)-depth_0(z,x)| <= Delta_t+C t.

Pure-base caps are controlled by Delta_t alone. There are finitely many bases outside I, each with a strict old maximum-depth gap below Q_0, so that gap persists. The new raw maximum is EXACTLY Q_0, while M(t)>M. Consequently Q_0/M(t)<Q_0/M.

Thus every unrestricted ordinary normalized-depth local minimum satisfies

    P subset union_(p in I) F_p.                      (A6)

This is a necessary geometric property, not a parity payment bound. The perturbation need not preserve a chosen compact normalization or the old minor quotas. Those are compactness tools, not constraints on the unrestricted competitor class. If desired, reapply a common continuous affine normalization; it preserves normalized ordinary depth and the integer bases. All statements can be made in the inherited relative base lattice, with the usual rank repair when an ambient full-dimensional representative is required.

## 5. Consequence for unrestricted global buffered minima

Suppose the globally attained logarithmic buffered minima at epsilon_j down to zero are normalized into the compact original bad sublevel, with positive limiting fibers, and suppose the uniform bound (6) for h_j holds. Let beta_* be the unrestricted ordinary minimum on this base. The constant parameter L=1 is admissible and its buffer is O(epsilon) at any fixed ordinary minimizer. Hence

    beta_* <= beta_epsilon^* <= beta_*+C epsilon.     (A7)

Every normalized body limit therefore attains beta_*. A subsequential sampled concave limit h of the bounded h_j gives a limiting physical buffer by the interior-core/boundary-collar argument in Section 1. Its maximum raw depth is the ordinary maximum Q_0=beta_* M, by (A7) and the all-normal slab comparison.

At every ordinary deepest mark, ordinary depth is positive, so the mark is in its own fiber interior. If h were positive there, (A2) would make its limiting buffered depth greater than Q_0. This is impossible. Thus every ordinary deepest base belongs to the zero-fiber set Z of h.

If h were nonzero on some sampled fiber u, nonnegative sampled concavity implies that u is outside the minimal face of EVERY zero base. In particular u satisfies (A4). The exact enlargement then contradicts ordinary minimality of the limit body. Therefore h is identically zero on every sampled fiber.

Finally the opposite-inner-ball estimate gives max_(K_(j,z)) h_j ->0 on each base. A subsequence contradiction proves the full statement

    sup_(sampled S_j) epsilon_j^(d+1) L_j ->0.         (A8)

This conclusion uses global buffered minimality through (A7), original shape minimality through (A6), and the proved compactness/positive-set bound. It does NOT use the contact martingale, source-weight splitting, or the finite-PL boundary upgrade. It implies uniform vanishing of physical buffers on this sequence. It is neither a Gamma payment nor an automatic differentiability or regularity theorem for the remaining critical caps.

The same proof applies when the chosen pairs are only o(1)-optimal for the global joint values: (A7) is then used only in its limiting form. No rate of parameter optimality is needed, since the limiting body is still an attained ordinary global minimum and the limiting buffered maximum is still its original maximum. This does not apply to arbitrary fixed-body parameter optimizers.
